National Assembly
Upper House
Proceedings of the Twenty-third Session
Complete
Magh 19, 2082
Monday
Meeting Number - 4
Presided over by Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
The meeting of the National Assembly commenced at 13:23 hrs.
(13:23 hrs)
Speaker:- Honorable members, the proceedings will commence. I will provide time for the honorable members to speak during the Zero Hour. Each honorable member will be given one minute for the Zero Hour and Special Time. First, Honorable Member Kiran Babu Shrestha.
Honorable Mr. Kiran Babu Shrestha (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Speaker,
(13:23 hrs)
I wish to draw the attention of the house to the issue of Nepal's financial transactions. The International Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has placed Nepal on its grey list and given it a two-year period to exit. The action plan to exit this list was to be implemented within one year. It was mentioned that if the action plan was not implemented within one year, Nepal would not be able to exit the grey list. However, news reports indicate that Nepal's efforts have been insufficient, as stated by the FATF. It was also mentioned that Nepal was given up to two years to exit the grey list, but even after one year, the implemented action plan has not been effective. This was mentioned in the FATF's budget statement during their meeting in Paris, France, from October 20 to 24, 2025. I request that this matter be brought to the attention of the house by the government. Thank you.
Honorable Speaker: Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.
(13:24 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Speaker,
(13:25 hrs)
Sir, more than 30 members of the Federal Parliament and Provincial Assemblies, along with local level chiefs, have decided to contest the upcoming House of Representatives elections on February 12, resigning before the completion of their terms. The Constitution of Nepal, Articles 86, 177, and 215, stipulate terms of six years for members of parliament and five years for local chiefs, respectively. Like unfaithful and deceitful lovers, these honorable individuals have forgotten the promises made to the public and the oaths they took to the constitution, and have burdened the state treasury with billions of rupees by necessitating fresh elections. Therefore, Honorable Speaker, I strongly urge that the Constitution of Nepal and other election-related laws be immediately amended to prevent such fugitive politics, where individuals abandon their responsibilities before completion, and to make our legislative and parliamentary practices dignified. Thank you.
Honorable Speaker:- Honorable Member Rukmini Koirala.
(13:26 hrs)
Honorable Ms. Rukmini Koirala (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable Speaker,
(13:26 hrs)
Today, I stand in this esteemed house as a voice crying out for the suffering of thousands of women. Even today, many sisters, daughters, mothers, and granddaughters in our society are victims of fear, violence, and humiliation. While home should be the safest place, for many women, it has become a prison of suffering. Silence, shame, and fear still muzzle their voices. But today, this house must break that silence. Violence against women is not just a legal issue. It is a serious social crime connected to our societal thinking, culture, values, and beliefs. Today, we, the government, must not only enact strict laws for victimized women but also enforce them strictly. (...Time expired.)
Honorable Speaker:- Honorable Member Renu Chand.
(13:27 hrs)
Honorable Ms. Renu Chand (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):- Honorable Speaker,
(13:28 hrs)
Sir, the Health Insurance Program is a program that establishes citizens' access to quality healthcare. It reduces individual expenses during treatment. It is an important program of the Government of Nepal. However, this program has not been operating effectively. It needs to be made more effective. But this government has stopped the payment of health insurance claims. Financially disadvantaged citizens are facing the most problems due to the halt in the Health Insurance Program. Therefore, to maintain the public's trust in the state, I urge the government to make necessary improvements immediately and resume the payment of health insurance claims. Thank you.
Honorable Speaker:- Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota.
(13:28 hrs)
Honorable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Speaker,
(13:28 hrs)
Elections are scheduled for February 21, and the election code of conduct is in effect. Amidst the uncertainty following the Madhesh movement, the country's development and energy sectors have been significantly affected. Some construction and energy projects halted by the current government are now in limbo. Due to the election code of conduct and decisions, projects are stalled, causing problems for contractors, laborers, and investors. Bank interest rates are rising, costs are increasing, but the government is unclear. Through you, Mr. Speaker, I have a question for the government: Who will decide which projects should be stopped and which should continue? How will the economic and time losses incurred in these projects be compensated? How is the government investigating such projects? Who will bear the financial burden on the state treasury from the cancellation of projects? For how long will development be held hostage, entangled between the movement and its leadership? Thank you.
Honorable Speaker:- Honorable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini.
(13:29 hrs)
Honorable Ms. Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Speaker,
(13:30 hrs)
Sir, development and construction work is, and should be, a common endeavor for all. The previous government selected projects and allocated budgets, but work has not yet begun on many of them. We have repeatedly stated that 'Asare' development (development carried out only at the end of the fiscal year) is detrimental to the public and results in budget wastage. Despite our repeated warnings, I would like to know this government's stance on 'Asare' development this year, what it intends to do, and what it plans to convey, through this esteemed house. Thank you.
(13:30 hrs)
Honorable Speaker:- Honorable Member Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari.
Honorable Mr. Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):-
(13:30 hrs)
Honorable Speaker, in the past few days, there have been reports of increasing incidents of theft, robbery, murder, rape, and online fraud in various parts of the country, including the Kathmandu Valley. It is reported that the same gangs involved in theft, robbery, and looting on August 24, when they escaped from prison, are now active in robberies. The residents of the Kathmandu Valley are somewhat terrified by the fear of theft and robbery. LP gas shortages have also begun to appear in areas like Kirtipur and Kalanki. With elections approaching, the artificial scarcity of daily necessities and the price hikes are making life difficult for the public. I wish to draw the government's attention to this. Thank you.
Honorable Speaker:- Honorable members, the Zero Hour session for honorable members concludes here. A letter regarding the delegation of duties by the Office of the President has been received. I will now inform you of the contents of the letter.
His Excellency Ram Chandra Paudel, the President, will be leading a Nepali delegation to Japan at the friendly invitation of the Government of Japan to participate in the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Nepal and Japan. He is scheduled to depart on Magh 18, 2082 (February 1, 2026, Sunday) and will be away until Magh 21, 2082. During his absence, His Excellency the Vice President has been assigned to perform the duties of the President, in accordance with Article 67, Sub-section 2 of the Constitution of Nepal. Dated Magh 18, 2082. Dr. Hari Prasad Lamsal (Secretary).
Honorable members, I now invite Honorable Maya Prasad Sharma, Chairperson of the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee, to present the committee's report on the Immigration Act, 2049, and the delegated legislation made under the Act to the house.
Honorable Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee Chairperson Mr. Maya Prasad Sharma:-
(13:33 hrs)
Honorable Speaker, the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee, in the course of studying delegated legislation within its purview, decided to study and analyze the Immigration Act, 2049, and the delegated legislation made under it, and present a report with recommendations to the esteemed National Assembly. In the course of its study, the committee directly addressed the recently controversial issue of visit visa cases and studied this Act, the delegated legislation under it, and the decisions and directives made by the Government of Nepal related to immigration. It conducted field observations of the Immigration Department and the immigration office at Tribhuvan International Airport, and held discussions and interactions with representatives of concerned agencies to advance the study. During the field observation of the Immigration Department and Tribhuvan International Airport, the committee held discussions with the Director General and staff of the department and also observed the detention center within the department.
Similarly, during the observation of Tribhuvan International Airport, the committee held discussions and interactions with the staff of the immigration office there and representatives of the security agencies. The committee held discussions with the Honorable Home Minister, former Chief Secretary, the coordinator of the committee formed to provide suggestions for the reform of immigration administration, Mr. Shankar Das Bairagi, the Director General of the Immigration Department, and officials including the chief of the Tribhuvan International Airport Immigration Office. To conduct a preliminary study of the Immigration Act, 2049, and the delegated legislation under it, the committee assigned Advocate and former Constituent Assembly member Dr. Khim Lal Devkota, with the support of the Parliamentary Support Project. The committee further studied the preliminary report prepared by Khim Lal Devkota and, incorporating the suggestions of the honorable members, the committee secretariat revised the report. The report was approved by the committee meeting held on Magh 15, 2082, and it was decided to present it to the esteemed house.
Honorable Speaker, delegated legislation has been formulated by the Government of Nepal, provincial governments, local governments, autonomous organizations, and constitutional bodies. When these bodies exercise their delegated authority, it is important for the institutional development of good governance in the country if they fulfill their official duties, responsibilities, and accountability within the general principles, limits, values, and authority of delegated legislation. However, it is a paradox that when formulating delegated legislation, the Government of Nepal and all other bodies have been exercising delegated authority without regard for the principles, limits, values, and authority of delegated legislation, and without considering their official duties, responsibilities, and accountability. Similarly, the Government of Nepal has been proposing many substantive matters as delegated legislation when presenting bills to Parliament, and Parliament and its committees have been accepting them, leading to delegated...

There are plenty of substantive issues in legislation. On the one hand, this has fragmented the authority of the parliament to make laws, and on the other hand, it has negatively impacted the improvement of good governance. The best solution for this is for the parliament to control delegated authority during the process of passing bills. I wish to draw the attention of the parliament and parliamentary committees to this.

Honorable Chairperson, the Immigration Act of 2049 has excessive delegated authority. Serious issues such as visa, expulsion, investigation, and entry-exit have been delegated, leading to increased discretionary power and the possibility of its misuse. The executive branch also faces significant risks of abuse of power due to discretionary powers, weak parliamentary oversight, lack of public consultation, and inability to meet modern technological and international standards. While administrative discretion is an essential basis for state governance, its misuse has led to various forms of corruption and irregularities, causing consumers to suffer. The visit visa incident can be cited as an example of this.

Honorable Chairperson, not only during the amendment of the Immigration Act but also during the passage of any bill, it is necessary to redefine the scope of delegated authority, keep substantive matters in the act itself, and only procedural matters in regulations, and strictly enforce the provisions for registering delegated legislation, publishing it in the gazette, and submitting it to parliament as determined by the Legislation Act, 2081. When drafting delegated legislation, it is necessary to make parliamentary oversight effective, consult extensively with stakeholders, and update the act to be time-appropriate by including modern systems like e-visa and biometrics. The use of discretion is necessary, but it is essential to clarify in the law the basis, reasons, and justification for it.

Honorable Chairperson, I express my sincere gratitude to the Honorable Chairperson and the Honorable Vice-Chairperson for continuously providing guidance, suggestions, and direction to our committee. I also extend my heartfelt thanks on behalf of the committee to the honorable members who have actively participated in the committee, the honorable ministers and representatives of other stakeholders who provided suggestions during the report preparation phase, the Secretary-General of the Federal Parliament, the Secretary of the National Assembly, and all the civil servants of the secretariat, including the secretariat staff, security personnel, and media personnel.

Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present to the esteemed assembly the "Study Report on Immigration and Delegated Legislation, 2082" prepared by the Delegated Legislation Committee, concerning the Public Policy and Immigration Act, 2049 and the delegated legislation made thereunder. I request that the report be discussed in the assembly.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I now provide time to Honorable Kamala Panta, Chairperson of the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee, to present the proposal for discussion on the Study Report on National Integrity Policy, 2082.

Honorable Chairperson of the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee, Ms. Kamala Panta: Honorable Chairperson, the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee under the National Assembly, in order to support the regular work of the National Assembly, has conducted a detailed study on the need for a National Integrity Policy in relation to administrative reform and good governance promotion within its area of work and has prepared the "Study Report on National Integrity Policy, 2082", which has been presented to the esteemed assembly.

Honorable Chairperson, today I wish to briefly present some of my views to bring this presented report into discussion. Honorable Chairperson, good governance is indispensable for sustainable development, prosperity, and peace. Integrity is an important pillar of good governance. To enhance integrity, all public officials, employees, and citizens in the public, private, cooperative, and non-governmental sectors, as well as in public life, must adopt conduct in accordance with the constitution, laws, and sectoral and professional ethics of the country. The Nepali constitution's commitment to a socially just society is achieved primarily through good governance. It is necessary to make the public sector, among others, clean, capable, impartial, transparent, corruption-free, accountable, and participatory. Developing legal, policy, and institutional frameworks at all levels is essential to ensure good governance. Good governance cannot be guaranteed without establishing an integrity-based governance system. To eradicate corruption from its roots in the country, it is necessary to adopt preventive measures and implement promotional activities for administrative reform through a national integrity policy. Although the government has previously attempted to issue a National Integrity Policy, it has not yet been issued due to the lack of adequate consultation and consensus with stakeholders. Due to economic indiscipline, irregularities, and increasing corruption in the country, Nepal's image has not been good at the national and international levels.

Honorable Chairperson, various incidents and news such as the practice of mixing adulterants in food items, the purification campaign by the police in Terai, the news of students calling the District Education Officer to a school for surprise inspection in Khotang, the demand for compensation to customers and cancellation of licenses for service providers if phone and internet services are not good, pressure from businessmen to stop the sale of sugar to Salt Trading, the report by Transparency International calling open bribery in government offices, and the seizure of gold while the owner remains missing, have raised questions about the good governance of the state. Why does a contractor not build a road on time? Why do investigative agencies not investigate? Why is the service of service-providing agencies weak? How to formulate policies for accountability, transparency, and administrative reform? Who will formulate them? How to increase public participation in policy-making? These questions remain unanswered today. To address such irregularities, an integrity policy is essential for the effective implementation of laws, policies, strategies, and action plans implemented by the government. It is necessary to address various irregularities and anomalies in all sectors of national development, service delivery, and governance. As Nepal is a party to the United Nations Convention Against Corruption, it is also necessary to formulate and implement an integrity policy to fulfill the obligations created by the provisions of the convention.

Honorable Chairperson, to establish a culture of professionalism and honesty in governance and to build an integrity-based, ethical, cultured, civilized, and prosperous society, all sector organizations must issue codes of conduct according to their work nature and adhere to the rules of integrity. Moral education is necessary from school to create cultured and dutiful citizens. It is necessary to reform policies, laws, strategies/procedures, institutional and structural reforms, and strengthen professionalism and integrity in areas such as good governance management and administrative reform. Legal provisions must be made for appropriate action against those who do not follow the rules of integrity, and the rules must be enforced. Keeping this fact in mind, it is imperative to immediately issue a National Integrity Policy in an integrated manner to operate all sectors cleanly, healthily, competitively, and systematically.

Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the proposal that the "Study Report on National Integrity Policy, 2082" prepared by the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee be discussed in the esteemed assembly in accordance with Rule 159 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I now put the proposal for discussion on the Study Report on National Integrity Policy, 2082, to a decision. Honorable Secretary, honorable members who are in favor of this proposal will say "Yes" and honorable members who are against it will say "No".

Honorable members in favor of this proposal, say "Yes".
-"Yes"
Honorable members against this proposal, say "No".
No "No" voices were heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal to discuss the Study Report on National Integrity Policy, 2082, has been unanimously approved.

Honorable members, the discussion on the Study Report on National Integrity Policy, 2082, will now begin. Honorable members participating in the discussion should focus on the subject and express their views. Honorable members wishing to participate in the discussion are requested to submit their names within two minutes. Each honorable member participating in the discussion has been allocated a time of 3 minutes. First, Honorable Member Urmila Aryal.

Honorable Ms. Urmila Aryal (Communist Party of Nepal, Maoist Centre): (13:52 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, I request that the National Integrity Policy, 2082, which is now before us as a proposal, be passed. It is very relevant and, in the current situation, has involved a lot of effort, including discussions in provincial assemblies, to implement the integrity policy with long-term vision. The National Integrity Policy has been presented to the assembly today by our Chairpersons. A long-term vision needs to be developed for this, and its mission needs to proceed positively. The country needs to move forward in terms of integrity. The main perpetrators of corruption and abuse of authority are known by name; I would say that those who are appointed as chiefs are themselves involved in corruption scandals. Such incidents are happening in the country. Therefore, the commitment we have shown through various movements and people's struggles has brought us this far. However, when we go into government and the field of implementation, even when we make good policies, we always have weaknesses in their implementation. And whenever we start making appointments, we look for people who will make it easier for the government and make the work easier. This tendency to look for people who will make the work easier has actually led to a lack of good governance and widespread corruption in the country. Considering all these things, the National Integrity Policy is a traditional aspect of our culture. The culture that existed in our villages is also eroding. Therefore, regarding integrity, our Chairperson has already spoken at length and with great dedication. However, regarding integrity, moral education used to be taught, but now that moral education is not taught. When we make appointments, after going into government, people are allowed to do whatever they want to suit themselves. The situation of making appointments and becoming infamous is happening. Because of this, despite fighting many battles, holding movements, and expressing our commitments with high respect, we are gradually becoming corrupt, and integrity...

and have been removing them. Therefore, in order to implement the Code of Conduct policy everywhere and for this to be passed by this house as well, and now it will be implemented across the country. Currently, people who are chairpersons of various local levels are resigning and going to contest elections as MPs. This kind of character is now becoming evident. Therefore, we need to adopt this policy more strongly regarding moral education and ethical conduct, and because of this, from the ward level of the local government to the central government, from the government to our National Assembly, House of Representatives, whatever needs to be implemented will be appropriate. And Dr. Rajanath Pandey, the secretary of our committee, has worked very hard. As far as the discussion is concerned, it has taken place in all provinces. It has shown us a way, and we have ethical conduct as a tradition. That ethical conduct (Time is up.) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota. (13:54 hrs) Honorable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, the National Good Governance Policy, 2082, prepared by the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee, has studied the constitution, has 4 chapters, 17 points, 3 schedules, and in each sub-point of each article, for the overall development of the country, for sustainable development, prosperity, and peace, good governance is essential. It has attempted to clarify in a structured manner the necessary efforts, policies, laws, loyalty, accountability, responsibility, honesty, and duties. Article 3 of Chapter 3 has prepared the draft of the National Good Governance Policy, 2082. The chairperson of the committee, the members, the secretary of the committee secretariat, and all the staff have worked very hard to create this draft, which is very good and dynamic. I would like to inform you that it is welcome. I would also like to express my gratitude. In the background of this draft National Good Governance Policy, 2082, national and international context and introduction have been provided, and past efforts have also been mentioned, and many things have been included in it. National and international aspects have been included. Actually, due to the absence of this good governance policy, corruption has flourished. In 2005, the United Nations also issued a directive to member states with 8 points from the General Assembly in 2005. However, due to the lack of implementation of the Code of Conduct policy in our Nepal, corruption is rampant today. It has covered every sector, from diplomacy to the private sector, NGOs, INGOs, in every economic aspect, including education, health, and roads. I would like to earnestly request the government, through the Honorable Chairperson, to implement this as soon as possible, by issuing directives or in whatever way it can be implemented. Thank you, Namaste, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Tulasa Kumari Dahal. (13:58 hrs) Honorable Ms. Tulasa Kumari Dahal (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, we are discussing the study report on the Code of Conduct Policy, 2082, presented by the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee. I would like to thank the honorable chairperson Kamala Pant and the honorable members of the committee and the concerned parties. This report is timely. While the previous government had made commitments, a Code of Conduct policy could not be formed. Today, we are discussing the study report on the Code of Conduct in the National Assembly. This is a matter of happiness. In Nepali society, trust is diminishing. Morality, humanity, discipline, good traditions, and our original customs are becoming challenging and problematic. Unhealthy competition, inhumane behavior, good governance, and the proper implementation of law are not happening. Qualities like impartiality, honesty, respect, and self-acceptance are being overshadowed. The disease of corruption is spreading. If previously it was concentrated in the center, today it has spread to the provinces and local levels, and it seems to have become a competition. Unsettled arrears are not being cleared, and regulatory bodies themselves are found to be involved in corruption. It seems to be establishing itself as a social custom. Maintaining good conduct is possible only through the efforts of everyone. Efforts can be made by the three tiers of government, political parties, constitutional bodies, parliament, parliamentary committees, departments, and private sector structures. Along with the policy, laws need to be enacted, commitments need to be made, and those who do not follow the Code of Conduct policy need to be warned, and provisions for punishment and fines should also be made. Individuals who adopt the Code of Conduct policy should be evaluated and encouraged, respected, and those who adopt a simple life and high thinking should be praised. This practice also needs to be initiated. It is also necessary for responsible individuals, organizations, and structures, and individuals working in those structures, to commit to adopting the Code of Conduct policy. If those in positions of responsibility adopt the Code of Conduct policy, others can also follow. However, it is found that those holding high positions, those considered important individuals, and those in positions of responsibility are not following this policy. In society, there are the poor and the wealthy. For the wealthy, there is a tradition of respecting and praising them. It is our collective responsibility to follow transparency, discipline, and discretion in our work, and it is also necessary for us to make commitments from our respective positions. I also appeal to everyone to declare their commitment to following the Code of Conduct policy themselves, and I conclude my remarks by urging this house to pass this report. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Dr. Beduram Bhusal. (14:01 hrs) Honorable Dr. Beduram Bhusal (Communist Party of Nepal, Unified Socialist):- Honorable Chairperson, I believe that the National Good Governance Policy, 2082, presented by the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee after extensive research, is very important. Because good conduct is a very important issue for good governance. Good governance, transparency, and accountability are considered special aspects of modern democracy. Good conduct against corruption, if there is good conduct, there will be no corruption; if there is no good conduct, there will be corruption. We have become widespread. If we want to control corruption, adopting good conduct is mandatory. The honorable members have worked hard to prepare this report by incorporating all these aspects. I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to all the concerned staff members for their hard work. Regarding good conduct, it is believed that we must have two types of conduct: good conduct and two types of conduct. Financial conduct and moral conduct. If financial conduct and moral conduct are clean, pure, and unblemished, then other departments are also considered clean, pure, and unblemished. The Code of Conduct policy provides guidance for this. If we do not have a Code of Conduct policy, and if there are no legal arrangements in a simple form, it will not be possible to control corruption. Corruption does not happen in the absence of good conduct. In our customs and traditions, good conduct had great importance, but now we are underestimating that importance, and our systems of conduct, especially those that establish moral education, good conduct, and societal norms and practices, have all collapsed. Therefore, I request the house to pass it, and I also request that the government take initiatives to implement the suggestions and directives it has given. I bid farewell. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra. (14:03 hrs) Honorable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, the National Good Governance Policy Study Report, 2082, prepared by the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee with great effort and investment, is a national asset. From what I have understood, good conduct means good behavior, purity, and purity of mind, moral behavior, and character. The tests of good conduct are speaking the truth, not deceiving, remaining disciplined, being restrained, and continuously trying to stay away from anger, greed, and attachment. Being helpful to others, using polite and civilized language is good conduct. Why is good conduct necessary? Because a person becomes virtuous, peace and harmony prevail in society, corruption and crime decrease, the moral standard of the nation becomes strong, and respect for the country increases worldwide. What are the rules of good conduct? Not planning for bribes and commissions, not cultivating deceit and hassle, respecting citizens, obeying laws and regulations with simplicity. Good conduct makes human life, individuals, society, and the nation prosperous, clean, and trustworthy. Now, along with this policy, there is a need for its operation, regulation, and oversight, but in our opinion, a change in thinking is also necessary. Irregularities in flying in government aircraft and irregularities in buying aircraft may be of different sizes, but the type seems to be similar. Can we learn any behavior from Chanakya? Chanakya had a shortage of oil in the past. Chanakya used two lamps. He would light one lamp when doing government work, and another lamp for his household work. Are we using government vehicles only for government work? As a small example, this report states that smoking is harmful to health, but there is no restriction on its production, distribution, and consumption. Nor are smokers looked down upon. Similarly, we talk about good conduct, but have we been able to insult those who do not practice good conduct? I feel that those who write and speak about good conduct are those who have not had the opportunity to engage in corruption. Thank you, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Sumitra B.C. (14:07 hrs) Honorable Ms. Sumitra B.C. (Communist Party of Nepal, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, today the Chairperson of the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee has presented the National Good Governance Policy, 2082 report to the house, and we are discussing good conduct. I wholeheartedly support this report, which has been prepared by the committee and brought forth with great effort by the committee secretariat, and which, after discussing not only within the committee but also with all the committees in the National Assembly, has concluded that there is a need for a National Good Governance Policy and that this policy must be passed. I believe it will be passed by this house. This report contains information about past activities and what needs to be done in the future regarding good conduct. The elders have already spoken. We say one thing and do another. If we oppose individual behavior, we can naturally move towards implementation by making this policy. For that, from home, parents teach children, and in schools, moral education should be included in the curriculum, and where we carry responsibilities and take responsibilities, we...

When we fulfill what we have pledged during the oath-taking, it will give meaning to the National Integrity Policy. To achieve this, let us all move forward from our respective positions, and the tendency to blame each other and absolve oneself is a fatal trend, in my opinion. Until policies and laws are made in our country, things are not right in terms of practical implementation. We will also work on this. The Prime Minister of the then government has also come here today to pass this report. I believe he will also express his commitment to implement it. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Maya Prasad Sharma.
(14:10 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Maya Prasad Sharma (Communist Party of Nepal, Maoist Centre):
(14:11 hrs)
The Development, Economic Affairs and Public Policy Committee has presented a new experience to the House after discussions and debates through the National Integrity Policy Committee. I wish to support it wholeheartedly. I would like to extend my heartfelt thanks to its chairperson, secretary, and all honorable members. It has raised important issues such as honesty, integrity, transparency, accountability, impartiality, equal treatment, interest management, zero tolerance towards corruption, and timeliness. I think now we are in parliament. In this short time, our Honorable Home Minister is also here. As we enter from the gate, the dignity of the parliament is being undermined. Even upon entering, the situation is chaotic. The Integrity Policy should address this as well. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Ganga Kumari Belbase.
(14:14 hrs)
97
Honorable Ms. Ganga Kumari Belbase (Communist Party of Nepal, Maoist Centre):
(14:14 hrs)
Honorable Chairperson, today we are discussing the study report on the National Integrity Policy. The Development, Economic Affairs and Public Policy Committee prepared it. I would like to thank the honorable members for their hard work. In ancient philosophy, dharma, artha, kama, and integrity values are mentioned. We see good work and good results, and we also see bad work and structures not being built on time, and contracts being broken. Morality is a human quality, a dharma; ethical conduct is a practice, and unethical conduct is also a practice. Only by being ethical can we make our lives meaningful. The law is for everyone; it is said that the law does not distinguish between small and big, but we also see that the law is applied differently to the small and the big. The law related to political parties has been made, but we see discrimination and factionalism within political parties. We also see that women's leadership is not accepted. The country has been federalized for 10 years, but significant responsibility has not been fulfilled in institutionalizing federalism. Although the constitution aims for a socialist-oriented system, it is not seen to have contributed to the improvement of the economic and social living standards of the people.
Accountability for actions taken while in public office is not seen. When mistakes are made, instead of showing morality, self-defense, and resignation for major mistakes when necessary, such actions are not seen. Those in power are expected to uphold fundamental principles like the rule of law, transparency, honesty, impartiality, and accountability, but morality is not demonstrated. Similarly, in public administration, transparency, financial accountability, a simple procurement system, and the establishment of mechanisms to control corruption are needed. The principle of working without expecting results should be adopted, and a system of providing work according to merit and pay according to work should be implemented. The strengthening of the federal structure requires development expenditure growth, discipline, and accountability. The government has also formed a committee under the leadership of a secretary following the Janji Andolan to advance this work. With the two-month work period given to this committee and everyone taking directives, the work has moved forward. I hope that today's report draft will be passed, and I conclude my remarks. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Kiran Babu Shrestha.
(14:17 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Kiran Babu Shrestha (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson,
(14:17 hrs)
As integrity, good governance, and honesty become scarce in Nepali society, immorality, moral degradation, and corruption are widespread. Corruption has become Nepal's number one challenge. In this context, to address this challenge, not just now, but as early as 2074 BS, the National Integrity Policy, 2074, was introduced, but it is unknown where it went or where it got lost. It is urgent now. This widespread immorality, this widespread corruption seen across Nepal, this indiscipline – the report presented here by the Development, Economic Affairs and Public Policy Committee after studying the Integrity Policy is extremely relevant. And at this juncture, by adopting this report, I urge the Government of Nepal to internalize this report and bring forth the Integrity Policy soon. Also, if the Integrity Policy had been introduced on time, would Nepali society have become so weak? Would Nepali society have become so undisciplined? A few days ago, some time ago, a few months ago, would national properties like Singha Durbar, our parliament building, the Supreme Court, have been burned down? Or if the National Integrity Policy had been introduced earlier and instilled in their minds, would the ministers who claim to hold fair elections not have absconded and gone to fight elections under the flag of some party today? For this reason too, the Integrity Policy is extremely necessary, so I urge the government to bring it soon. And in the Integrity Policy, it is not just about knowing; it is about gaining knowledge. The most important thing is how much can be implemented in practice. Knowledge and wisdom are different aspects, in my opinion. Just acquiring knowledge is not enough. If we do not apply that knowledge with wisdom, that knowledge remains just knowledge. We have seen many learned, highly educated people, intellectual personalities, who have acquired a lot of knowledge, but where have they applied their knowledge? We have seen knowledge used for killing people, against society, against social welfare. Therefore, to use this knowledge correctly, wisdom is also needed. I request that the Integrity Policy be brought soon and move forward in that direction. Thank you, Jai Nepal.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Rukmini Koirala.
(14:20 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Rukmini Koirala (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honorable Chairperson,
(14:20 hrs)
Today, we are expressing our views and discussing the report on the Integrity Policy. The Development, Economic Affairs and Public Policy Committee has prepared this report very well, and I wish to welcome and support it. However, what I feel is that this report contains materials needed to implement the Integrity Policy under 49/50 headings. If the Integrity Policy is considered and followed in all these headings, it would not take long for the country to develop. If responsibility for implementation is given in seven laws, and if the three-tiered governments, political parties, constitutional bodies, parliament, parliamentary committees, various departments, revenue investigation, asset purification, industry and commerce, non-state structures, non-governmental private sectors, civil society, media, the National Vigilance Centre, the National Information Commission, the Public Procurement Monitoring Office, the Social Welfare Council, and other such institutions follow it, the country will transform itself. It is seen that Nepal ranked first in the increase of corruption in the first year. It is dire. In the last five years, development work has been done that has never happened in Nepal before. It is also necessary to assess what work was done during the tenure of which government in the past. Now, implementing the Integrity Policy is extremely necessary. In the suggestions, a budget of 1 kharba 18 arba has been allocated for major national pride projects, and there are other budgets as well. This was during the previous governments, but because contractors do not work on time, delay work, and repeatedly get extensions, leading to scandals, party leaders have had to face public criticism. Parliament makes policies, but the practice of political parties showing the way to civil servants and civil servants showing the way to political parties in policy implementation must end, and everyone must implement the Integrity Policy for the country to develop on its own. The government, private sector, political parties, civil society, and individuals must achieve self-purification of integrity. I wish for this report to be passed. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.
(14:23 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson,
(14:23 hrs)
Among the main demands of the Janji Andolan on Bhadra 23 and 24 was the end of corruption and the establishment of good governance in the country. Today, I am extremely happy that the Prime Minister, the head of the government formed on the foundation of that movement, is participating in this discussion in the National Assembly for the first time, possibly sitting with us. I am reminded of the sessions before the 23rd. Honorable Chairperson, specifically, the Prime Minister's commitment to holding elections for the House of Representatives on Falgun 21 will be of special value in Nepal's history, I believe. While discussing the Integrity Policy presented by the Development, Economic Affairs and Public Policy Committee, its draft came as early as 2074 BS. Due to various reasons, that policy could not be passed, and now the committee has brought this report. This report comes with the latest status of good governance in Nepal, the good and improvable aspects of the main bodies of the Government of Nepal for establishing good governance, existing laws for promoting good governance, the need for an Integrity Policy, and a framework for an Integrity Policy. I have found this report to be very commendable. Some policies included in this report, especially for the development of the common citizen's morality and the promotion of moral values, do not seem to have taken clear policy strategies on how to become happy and respected or how to build them. We need to see whether it is appropriate to place the legislature and the bureaucracy together in sectoral strategies. Are policies and strategies sufficient, or do laws need to be made for this? We need to look into this. We are on the grey list, corruption is increasing, and we have obligations under the Convention against Corruption. Therefore, I request that this report be passed by the House as soon as possible and that the relevant ministry advance this policy, and the committee pass it. Finally, while elections are happening in the country, we need to see if the government has been able to show results of integrity, good governance, and social justice in service delivery. We also need to see if the Government of Nepal has made any decisions that are perceived as bad governance and that directly or indirectly affect Nepali citizens in the election process and system. Therefore, I request that this report be passed and moved forward. Thank you.
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.

(2:26 PM) Honorable Mr. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):- (2:26 PM) Respected Chairperson, the Honorable Chairperson Kamala Pant of the Development, Economic Affairs and Public Governance Committee has presented the Report on the National Integrity Policy, 2082, before us, and it has been proposed for discussion in the House. This important document has come before us. This document seeks to encompass many things. I believe that the issues of justice, honesty, trust, and discipline in this integrity policy are important matters that need to be established. Yesterday, how much did we trust? Why has our trust been broken today? We need to analyze this. Looking at the prevalence of corruption, which is a matter for discussion here, in 2080/081, if we look at complaints from local levels, more than nineteen thousand complaints have been filed with the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority. From this, we can easily understand that corruption has flourished from the bottom to the top. The top blames the bottom, and the bottom blames the top. Are we honest? Why has this bridge between us been broken? Why has trust been broken? If we can be honest from top to bottom, if we can be loyal, if we can keep ourselves disciplined, then everyone will praise us, I believe. And to improve this, whether it is the parliamentary committee, the judicial council, constitutional bodies, or the vigilance center, all of them have an important role to play, I believe. And we are observing, especially during times of crisis. The changes that occur in our lives, the changes seen in people's lives, the unnatural changes, make people in society think of themselves in the same way and look at them with the eyes of a corrupt person. Because of this, we feel that the impact on our daily lives has also been affected. Today, the Prime Minister is also with us. In the context of the dignity of this National Assembly, which is inclusive, representing Dalits and women, I heard from the ministers themselves that their personal secretaries took files and engaged in corruption. We saw this in the Parliament. We found it difficult to digest this word. This matter has caused us pain. We do not want to say this word. Respected Chairperson: Honorable Member Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari. (2:29 PM) Honorable Mr. Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):- (2:30 PM) Respected Chairperson, I wish to express my views on the study report, 2082, regarding the National Integrity Policy for good governance. According to data released by the Global Corruption Barometer Asia 2020, corruption in Nepal has increased to 58 percent in the last year. Complaints received by Hello Sarkar, complaints filed with the Office of the Attorney General, complaints related to property, complaints related to foreign exchange offenses, and the data of court judgments in the Supreme Court do not present a satisfactory situation. The Auditor General's report also points out that this data is not satisfactory. The slogan of good governance and integrity has remained limited to speeches; practical application and satisfactory results have not been felt. However, from the perspective of public concern and state accountability, the steps taken resolutely by the 18-month government against corruption had instilled some hope in the public. It would be even better if the report mentioned how the files under investigation for corruption and irregularities were stopped at that time, keeping good governance at the center. Regarding administrative reform, due to the absence of a National Integrity Policy, the report has been prepared with considerable effort, considering the increasing malpractices, irregularities, corruption within the state and society, and their impact on the general public, based on field studies, interactions at the provincial and local levels, and international experiences, including the six-point directive specified in Article 8 of the United Nations Convention Against Corruption, implemented by the UN General Assembly since 2005. I welcome and support this report. The image of Nepal has been clearly tarnished internationally due to economic irregularities, indiscipline, lack of transparency, and corruption in the country. There is a need for moral conduct, self-purification, transparency, and accountability. This report highlights the need for moral education. Through you, Respected Chairperson, I request the government to pass this report from this respected assembly and formulate an integrity policy in accordance with this report. Thank you and greetings. Respected Chairperson: Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima". (2:32 PM) Honorable Ms. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):- (2:33 PM) Respected Chairperson, first of all, I express my heartfelt thanks to the Development, Economic Affairs and Public Governance Committee for drawing attention to the much-needed integrity. I especially thank Chairperson Honorable Kamala Pant and the committee family for their success in this task. The committee, with the participation of all stakeholders, has conducted a deep study and prepared a very important study report on the National Integrity Policy, which is essential for the country. In Nepali society, which has a history of high Nepali culture, morality is fading. It would not be an exaggeration to say that there is a drought of sorts. This is a matter of great concern for us. In such a situation, I believe this report will serve as a guiding star for building an integrity-filled Nepali society. Respected Chairperson, integrity is a moral quality based on truth, justice, conduct, honesty, politeness, self-control, and duty. Integrity is moral conduct through which an individual upholds truth, honesty, and social responsibility in their thoughts, words, and actions. Whatever behavior is correct, moral, and better for society is integrity. Although issues like morality and honesty are matters that individuals must practice themselves, it is necessary to have an integrity policy to uphold and inspire the common moral responsibility and practical integrity for everyone in the construction of public and personal life and in the performance of duties in the public life of public servants. The need for an integrity policy arises due to the weakness of the practice of working based on systems. Respected Chairperson, the objective of the integrity policy in all sectors, including the public sector, is to control corruption, ensure transparency in administration, maintain public trust and confidence, increase moral values, and prevent wrong conduct. That is, to work according to the constitution, laws, and moral values. It means staying away from bribes and corruption, demonstrating political impartiality, maintaining government confidentiality, not misusing power, properly utilizing government property, not taking undue benefits, behaving with dignity and respect, and not making statements that spread confusion in society by those holding public office. However, here, efforts are made to raise public hope by saying that corruption can be controlled in five days, and by blaming those in power for not doing so, further anger is generated. But when those who are supposed to act reach the place of action, those who are corrupt and immoral are given impunity and are spared. Respected Chairperson, making public the asset details of individuals holding public office falls under the integrity policy, but we are not following this policy. If a decision is made not to make asset details public through consultation, we are citizens of the country. Ministers at the electoral level, without fulfilling their duties, are seen to be evading their moral obligations in the pursuit of becoming MPs and Prime Ministers, and are rushing to contest elections. This is also seen in the ministers of the current non-political government. There is a tendency to make rules for accepting and giving gifts favorable to oneself. Respected Chairperson, there is no connection between the worker and the representative anywhere; this is why an integrity policy is needed, Respected Chairperson. Respected Chairperson: Honorable Members, the order of speaking on the discussion of the National Integrity Policy Study Report, 2082, ends here. Honorable Members, now I will provide time for the Respected Prime Minister Shushila Karki to answer the questions raised in the discussion. Respected Prime Minister Ms. Shushila Karki:- Before addressing this, first, I would like to address the Chairperson with one or two things later. This is my first time in life that such an opportunity has come. It has come due to circumstances, not by choice. I don't think so. I didn't seek it; circumstances forced me to come. And now, this opportunity that I have received here, perhaps it will be difficult to get it again in life, and I don't expect to get it. I have also gained this experience. I have been to the House very few times. I have been to the House of Representatives as well. After becoming the Chief Justice or a judge, for nine years, which was my valuable time, I could never go during that period. The question of going did not even arise. The Chief Justice does not go to the government's side for this or that. Today, I am happy that I have this opportunity and this time has supported me to come to this point in my life, which is a good experience. I also got the opportunity to see this and speak at this time. Now I will start my points. Respected Chairperson, as the Prime Minister of the interim government formed on the basis of the movement led by the youth on Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082, I feel a serious sense of responsibility as a witness to a historic turning point by being present and speaking a few words in this esteemed meeting of the National Assembly. I congratulate the individuals elected in the recently concluded National Assembly elections. Similarly, I congratulate the honorable members who are completing their terms and are about to retire, and I wish them a happy future life. On the day I became Prime Minister, i.e., Bhadra 27, 2082, in line with the spirit of the youth movement, to normalize the then situation, prevent further conflict in the country, stop loss of life and property, and bring the state back to its constitutional track, I had recommended to the Respected President the dissolution of the then House of Representatives on Falgun 21, 2082. I wish to inform this respected assembly that, as per that recommendation, the House of Representatives has been dissolved, and the elected government is eager to be empowered by holding elections in a free, fair, and credible environment at the stipulated time. I pay respect to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the Jenji movement in this assembly and express deep sorrow for the irreparable loss suffered by the martyrs' families. I also wish a speedy recovery to the injured in the movement. I have stated on various occasions before that I have not become Prime Minister with any ambition for governance or desire for any position. I have taken the responsibility of Prime Minister in a difficult situation based on the request of the change-seeking youth, discussions with political parties, and the Respected President, to bring the disrupted constitutional system back on track and save the country from crisis. Respected Chairperson, the rebellion led by the youth on Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082, was a reflection of the consciousness against the insensitivity of our rulers towards youth aspirations and the widespread corruption and state governance in the country. Based on the spirit and intention of the constitution, the weaknesses in the areas of good governance, prosperity, and development, and the dissatisfaction, deprivation, or neglect arising from them.

We must accept that the movement was born. That movement is also a result of our inability to live up to the democratic values and norms, including the current constitution. This rebellion is a mirror in which our own governmental flaws and behavioral weaknesses are reflected. The Nepali youth generation, aware of the miraculous development in information technology, aspires for equal access to state resources and opportunities, employment, and a quality life in their own country. These aspirations are not just for the youth but are essential prerequisites for Nepal's economic transformation. Therefore, it is too late for all three organs of the state – the executive, the legislature, and the judiciary – to diligently work towards fulfilling those aspirations. This is why we have had to bear great losses. The current government has declared the warriors who sacrificed their lives in the Gen Z movement as martyrs, provided relief to the concerned families, and prioritized the treatment and livelihoods of the injured. A historic agreement has been reached between the government and the representatives of the movement to address the demands of the movement, changing the political direction of the country. The government is fully committed to making the work of public bodies transparent and accountable and to reducing corruption. I wish to inform you that the preparation of the strategic plan and technology-based good governance roadmap for corruption reduction is in its final stages. The nomination of candidates for the House of Representatives election to be held on February 21, 2082, has been completed, and state resources have been concentrated on the election. Most of the weapons looted during the movement have been recovered, and security has been fully guaranteed. Integrated election security has been approved and implemented. All security mechanisms have been ensured to operate. The participation of political parties and various candidates seen in the election, as well as the enthusiasm of the public, demonstrates the faith, belief, and commitment of the Nepali people towards democracy. This election is not just a regular process of sending representatives to the parliament; it must become a starting point for a new political culture of the Nepali nation. Therefore, I humbly appeal to all sides through this esteemed house to fully adhere to the election code of conduct and to conduct the upcoming election in a clean and impartial environment. It has been possible to normalize the situation and create this environment for the election with the cooperation and goodwill of the federal government, provincial and local governments, the Election Commission, political parties, leaders and representatives of the Gen Z movement, civil society, the diplomatic community, and the media. For this, I highly appreciate the understanding of all parties through the esteemed chairperson. Today, we discussed the National Integrity Policy. I am confident that this will be an important document for creating a corruption-free Nepal in the future. However, integrity is not maintained merely by speeches, sermons, or the decorative arrangement of beautiful words in documents; it is something that each of us must embody. The main issue raised by the youth in the Gen Z movement is a society free from corruption, good governance, and integrity. Since the formation of this government, we have prioritized frugality. Therefore, the misuse of resources has been stopped to a great extent. We have not taken unnecessary facilities. We have not exerted any undue pressure on public bodies and regulatory institutions. These bodies are working with full professional freedom in accordance with the law. Some results are visible now, and we have laid the foundation for some to be seen in the long term. Taking this year's events as a lesson, we must all always be vigilant so that citizens do not have to come to the streets in the future for good governance. For this, we must not be engrossed in the lust for power but must have unwavering commitment to the rule of law. Currently, we do not have a House of Representatives, but a House of Representatives elected by the true mandate of the people is coming. We have the National Assembly. It is considered an institution of wise individuals. The government will respect the directives issued by this permanent house, which plays a mature and judicious role in the interest of the country. Finally, in this final phase of my short tenure, I want to assure you that we have repaired broken institutions and sown the seeds of new hope. I urge all bodies to unite and work without delay to resolve structural causes such as widespread corruption, impunity, and injustice in the country. I also want to express my opinion on a matter that has been raised here. You may be aware that I took my oath of office on the 27th. After that, the Council of Ministers was not formed for some time. This is because we are not from political parties; political parties have their own members. We had to find people from outside for the interim government. In that context, there was significant pressure from Gen Z. People from Gen Z came saying they should be ministers, and names like Mahabir Pun and Kulman Ghising were pressured. We were in a situation where we had to agree. Then many names came, and we brought some of them into the Council of Ministers. At that time, these personalities were not supposed to come to the Council of Ministers. But the pressure from Gen Z was that you must take them. You must take Kulman. You must take Pun, and you must take other state ministers. Such voices were heard. And I, specifically, not others, I specifically, joined my hands and said, 'As long as you are going to stay, please stay, because there is pressure from Gen Z. It won't happen otherwise.' Then names like Bablu Ghimire also came from Gen Z. Now, they have become state ministers, and Bablu and others are also somewhat popular figures. We also knew that they were people who would enter politics. Deceit occurs where someone contests elections while being in government; it can be said that they acted deceitfully in the interim government. But a person who has left the government, to whom we have given the word that the day you go to contest elections, resign and go, we will bid you farewell. But as long as you have to stay, it is because of the voice of Gen Z. Sudhan Gurung even embraced Pun and brought him. He was brought up from the streets while selling books. So, I don't think anyone has left. State ministers like Bablu Ghimire are there. Now, because they are of the Gen Z type in this changed context, they cannot contest elections. I don't think that's the case. And frankly, if you want to assign blame, blame me. Do not blame them. Because I had given the word to form the government at that time, I had told Kulmanji too, 'The day you are going, I will bid you farewell. Go, contest elections comfortably.' I had said that. Therefore, I don't think they acted deceitfully or politically. It is useless to say that. They have their lives, their own lives. They have their own age, their own culture to enter politics. Therefore, just because they went that way, I have clarified to you that I gave my word. There was pressure from Gen Z; they had to be brought in. There was pressure from them; they said they would leave when they wanted. Therefore, they left. Even today, they have no contact with the Council of Ministers, nor have they made any demands. Even today, we have no contact with them by phone. They went into the elections. They have participated in the elections. I don't feel the need to say anything otherwise. As for Pun, he left in anger. There were a couple of laws to be made. Those laws were good. But we could not help him by making those laws in this short period. That law was for the country, but we could not help him. There are various circumstances; not everything happens. Therefore, it is the right of an individual whether to enter politics or not. So, it is useless to say that. This accusation also came that this person is from the Rastriya Swatantra Party. Two people went to the Rastriya Swatantra Party. Kulmanji belongs to his own party. If Mahabir Pun does not have a party, then not everyone has gone to the Rastriya Swatantra Party. And we have no such contact with anyone. This is wrong; this is a false narrative. It is their own right. We asked everyone about the elections. We asked, 'Do you need anyone?' Those who did not want to go stayed. Those who had no political interest. We knew this person was interested; we knew that person was interested. They came under the pressure of Gen Z. They came and went. They left properly. They have no contact even now. We honored them with garlands and said, 'As long as you worked here, even if just drinking tea, you worked.' They probably drank two cups of tea from the ministry daily. 'You have left. Thank you. We have sent you off.' I will conclude here by saying this. I am happy to have had the opportunity to speak today. Thank you for this opportunity. It is very difficult to get such an opportunity again. It is difficult, and I don't expect it. I am not from that field. It is not my nature, nor my culture. I have never been a member of a political party. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the discussion on the report regarding the National Integrity Policy, 2082, is concluded here. Honorable members, based on the issues raised by the honorable members in the discussion and the views expressed by the honorable Prime Minister in response, I direct the Government of Nepal to implement the suggestions included in the National Integrity Policy Study Report, 2082, on a priority basis. Honorable members, as no notice has been received from the honorable members regarding the rejection of the ordinance under Rule 89 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, I grant permission to the honorable Home Minister, Om Prakash Aryal, to present the proposal for the approval of the Ordinance to Amend the Voter List Act, 2073, 2082, under Rule 92, Sub-rule 3 of the same rules. Honorable Home Minister Mr. Om Prakash Aryal: Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present to this esteemed assembly the proposal for the approval of the Ordinance to Amend the Voter List Act, 2073, 2082. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I now put to vote the proposal presented by the honorable Home Minister Om Prakash Aryal for the approval of the Ordinance to Amend the Voter List Act, 2073, 2082. Honorable members in favor of this proposal will say 'Aye'. - 'Aye' Honorable members against this proposal will say 'Nay'. No 'Nay' voices were heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal for the approval of the Ordinance to Amend the Voter List Act, 2073, 2082, has been unanimously approved. Honorable members

In accordance with Rule 89 of the National Assembly Rules of Procedure, 2075, as no notice has been received from Honourable Members regarding the rejection of any ordinance, I grant permission to the Honourable Home Minister, Om Prakash Aryal, to present a proposal to approve the first amendment ordinance to the House of Representatives Election Act, 2082, in accordance with Sub-rule 3 of Rule 92 of the same Rules of Procedure.

Honourable Home Minister Mr. Om Prakash Aryal:- Respected Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present before this esteemed assembly the proposal to approve the first amendment ordinance to the House of Representatives Election Act, 2082. Thank you.

Respected Chairperson:- Honourable Members, I now put to vote the proposal presented by the Honourable Home Minister, Om Prakash Aryal, to approve the first amendment ordinance to the House of Representatives Election Act, 2082. Honourable Members in favour of this proposal will say "Aye". Honourable Members in favour of this proposal will say "Aye". "Aye". Honourable Members against this proposal will say "Nay". The "Nay" sound was not heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal to approve the first amendment ordinance to the House of Representatives Election Act, 2082, has been unanimously approved.

Honourable Members, in accordance with Rule 89 of the National Assembly Rules of Procedure, 2075, as no notice has been received from Honourable Members regarding the rejection of any ordinance, I grant permission to the Honourable Home Minister, Om Prakash Aryal, to present a proposal to approve the Nepal Special Service Act (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2082, in accordance with Sub-rule 3 of Rule 92 of the same Rules of Procedure.

Honourable Home Minister Mr. Om Prakash Aryal:- Respected Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present before this esteemed assembly the proposal to approve the Nepal Special Service Act (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2082. Thank you.

Respected Chairperson:- Honourable Members, I now put to vote the proposal presented by the Honourable Home Minister, Om Prakash Aryal, to approve the Nepal Special Service Act (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2082. Honourable Members in favour of this proposal will say "Aye". Honourable Members in favour of this proposal will say "Aye". "Aye". Honourable Members against this proposal will say "Nay". The "Nay" sound was not heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal to approve the Nepal Special Service Act (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2082, has been unanimously approved.

Honourable Members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Friday, Falgun 23, 2082, at 1:15 PM. This meeting is hereby adjourned. (Thereafter, the meeting was adjourned to be held on Friday, Falgun 23, 2082, at 1:15 PM.)

sections.summary_en: Several members raised issues during the Zero Hour. Kiran Babu Shrestha discussed Nepal's FATF grey list status. Padam Bahadur Pariyar criticized politicians resigning before their term ends. Rukmini Koirala spoke about violence against women. Renu Chand addressed issues with the Health Insurance Program. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota raised concerns about stalled development projects due to the election code of conduct. Bishnu Devi Pudasaini questioned the government's approach to 'Asare' development. Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari highlighted rising crime rates and artificial scarcity.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Urmila Aryal supports the passage of the National Integrity Policy, 2082, highlighting its relevance and the need for long-term vision. She discusses the prevalence of corruption and abuse of authority, the erosion of traditional values, and the decline in moral education, urging for effective implementation of the policy.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The discussion continued on the National Good Governance Policy, 2082. Several members highlighted the importance of the policy in combating corruption and promoting ethical conduct. They emphasized the need for its effective implementation across all levels of government and society, and suggested measures such as legal enforcement and public awareness campaigns.

sections.summary_en: Honorable Rajendra Laxmi Gaire initiated a discussion on the Report on the National Integrity Policy, 2082, highlighting concerns about the prevalence of corruption and the erosion of trust. Honorable Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari presented statistics on rising corruption and supported the report, urging its passage. sections.summary_en: The discussion on the National Integrity Policy Study Report, 2082, concluded. The Prime Minister, Shushila Karki, was then invited to respond to the issues raised.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The discussion revolved around the aftermath of a movement, the government's response to its demands, and the upcoming elections. The speaker highlighted the government's efforts in declaring martyrs, providing relief, and reaching an agreement with movement representatives. The importance of transparency, accountability, and good governance was emphasized, along with the upcoming elections and the need for public participation. The speaker also addressed the formation of the Council of Ministers, the pressure from the Gen Z movement, and the departure of some ministers to contest elections, clarifying their actions and taking responsibility.

Subsequently, a proposal to approve the Nepal Special Service Act (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2082, was also presented and unanimously approved.
